verdict.rationale: Amazon SES is used programmatically by design. Its docs describe sending through an AWS SDK, the SMTP interface, or direct API calls, with IAM controlling access, so headless, non-interactive automation is directly supported. However, nothing in the evidence addresses CI pipelines specifically. Missing for 10: documented CLI or CI usage, guidance on CI credentials or non-interactive auth, and independent hands-on corroboration of CI automation.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: you can send email from Amazon EC2 by using an AWS SDK, by using the Amazon SES SMTP interface, or by making calls directly to the Amazon SES API
You can use the Amazon SES API v2 to send the following types of messages: Simple ... Raw ... Templated
Control user access to your email sending by using AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM).
